en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, which are divided into three main geographical regions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers across Laguna and Rizal provinces.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, spanning 14,649 square kilometers and containing over 1,700 islands.
Mount Mayon in Albay features a near-perfect cone reaching 2,462 meters high and has recorded over 50 eruptions in the last 400 years.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, plunging to a maximum recorded depth of 10,540 meters at the Galathea Depth.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world with a wingspan reaching up to two meters.
Due to its location in the Pacific typhoon belt, the Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones every year.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into steep mountains reaching up to 1,500 meters in elevation and are over 2,000 years old.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 96,828 hectares of protected marine habitat located in the center of the Sulu Sea.
